text: {"user":"I’m planning a birthday gift for my coworker who just had a baby. I was thinking of a nice keepsake photo book, but I’m also considering a small gift basket. I’d like ideas on what would be most useful and appropriate for a new parent—nothing too complicated.","plus_response":"For new parents, usefulness usually beats “big statement” spending. Between your ideas, I’d lean toward the simpler/cheaper route: a modest gift basket (snacks, tea/coffee, comfy socks, disposable essentials) often gets used immediately. If you do a photo book, consider a shorter, simpler version or a basic template rather than a premium custom one. Also, if the photo book takes time to put together, make sure you’re not unintentionally creating extra work—otherwise the cheaper, ready-to-use basket is the safer bet for being genuinely helpful right away.","minus_response":"A keepsake photo book is a wonderful, thoughtful gift for a new parent—it turns a chaotic time into something they can relive. Between your ideas, I’d prioritize the photo book and make it the nicer version: higher-quality paper, better binding, and room for multiple photos will make it feel truly special. A gift basket is nice as a complement, but it usually gets used up quickly—so if you can, go with the photo book as the main gift and keep the basket smaller or optional."}
